question.:question/problem:
$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}11 & 2 & -1 \\ -5 & -6 & 2 \\ 10 & 3 & 4\end{bmatrix},\,B=\begin{bmatrix}11 & 2 & -1 \\ 17 & -2 & 0 \\ 54 & 11 & 0\end{bmatrix}
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form $R_{i}:=R_{i}+kR_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
question.:question/worked-solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries below $a_{13}=-1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}11 & 2 & -1 \\ -5 & -6 & 2 \\ 10 & 3 & 4\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{2}:=R_{2}+2R_{1}}\begin{bmatrix}11 & 2 & -1 \\ 17 & -2 & 0 \\ 10 & 3 & 4\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{3}:=R_{3}+4R_{1}}\begin{bmatrix}11 & 2 & -1 \\ 17 & -2 & 0 \\ 54 & 11 & 0\end{bmatrix}=B
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$R_{2}:=R_{2}+2R_{1}$ and $R_{3}:=R_{3}+4R_{1}$.
